intro: What the Bank of England Base Rate is, who sets it, how it feeds into mortgage, standard variable and savings rates, and where to see its history.
explanation:
Bank Rate is the interest rate the Bank of England sets for the UK, and it affects the level of other rates across the economy. The Bank pays interest at this rate to the banks and building societies that keep money with it, and charges it on any loans it makes to them. That is why it affects the rates banks themselves pay and charge, and through them what customers are offered.

## Bank Rate is not the rate on your mortgage or savings account

Lenders and savings providers set their own rates, and they follow Bank Rate in different ways. Savings rates usually move in the same direction as Bank Rate. A tracker mortgage is linked to an external rate such as Bank Rate, so it moves when that rate moves. A standard variable rate is typically set by the lender rather than tied to Bank Rate, so it need not change by the same amount or on the same day. A fixed rate stays the same for its term, so a change in Bank Rate doesn't reach it straight away, though it can affect the deals on offer when the term ends.

## The Monetary Policy Committee decides it at eight meetings a year

Bank Rate is decided by the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), whose job is to keep inflation low and stable. The committee meets eight times a year. At each meeting it decides whether to move Bank Rate or leave it where it is, aiming to get inflation to its target and hold it there.

## How a change in Bank Rate reaches prices

A change in interest rates alters what people can afford to spend, and that in turn shapes the prices businesses can charge. When Bank Rate is higher, loans cost more and savings earn more, so people and businesses tend to spend less and price rises slow down. When it is lower, the pattern reverses: borrowing is cheaper, saving pays less, spending picks up and prices tend to rise faster.

## The Bank publishes Bank Rate history back to 1694

The Bank publishes official Bank Rate history data going back to 1694, as a [downloadable spreadsheet](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/monetary-policy/baserate.xlsx). Its [online history table](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/Bank-Rate.asp) lists each change from 1975.
